feedback_request.compare_against: Iteration 8 (mass 0.5, y = 0.08): oval progress 0.12 and score 55.18. Iteration 7 (same design) gave oval progress 0.2725 and score 75.92. A matching result confirms the design is stable and that the mass 0.5 oval drop was real.

intent: Restore the iteration 7 geometry, the best design so far (score 75.92): mass 0.6 kg, forward lead y = 0.08 (the contract maximum), 16 mm sensors at x = -0.08 to 0.08 in 0.04 m steps, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body 0.16 by 0.14 m. Change nothing else. Integrator: keep kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, last_direction recovery and the 25-times-x weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2). Expected result: oval progress near 0.27, s-bend progress near 0.157, slalom progress near 0.109 with 1.0 line loss per run, giving a score near 76. This is a reproduction of the best known design and tests whether the result is stable.
learning: Evidence: the mass 0.5 step at y = 0.08 lost the oval gain (progress 0.2725 to 0.12) while keeping the s-bend (0.1644) and slalom (1.0 line loss) within limits. So the oval progress is non-monotonic in mass and sensitive to mass near 0.6 kg. Hypothesis A: the 0.6 kg result is reproducible, because the simulator is deterministic per seed and track. Hypothesis B: the oval gain is a narrow feature of mass 0.6 and y = 0.08 that any change will lose. If A holds, the design is the safe final-race candidate. If the oval result differs from 0.2725, the race has a seed or disturbance effect that the team should account for before making further changes.
rationale: Iteration 8 (mass 0.5, y = 0.08) scored 55.18, well below iteration 7 (mass 0.6, y = 0.08), which scored 75.92 and is the best design so far. The loss came from the oval. Oval progress fell from 0.2725 back to 0.12, the level seen in every earlier oval test, and oval score fell from 115 to 51. The s-bend improved to progress 0.1644 with oscillation 0.141, and slalom stayed at 1.0 line loss per run with progress 0.1075. So both pre-set hold rules passed (s-bend progress at or above 0.1573, slalom losses at or below 1.0), but the oval gain did not survive the lighter mass. Mass 0.5 is therefore not a monotonic improvement. The oval gain at y = 0.08 appears to depend on a specific mass band, and 0.6 kg is the only tested point inside it that scores well. Entity R1's rules for y = 0.08 were written for 0.5 kg and did not anticipate an oval collapse, so I am not following them further. The simulator is deterministic per seed and track, so the iteration 7 design can be restored exactly. Restoring it gives the best known score (75.92) and a reliable baseline for the final race. Further single-lever tests (for example wheel_track 0.11) remain open for later iterations if the team wants to explore beyond the known best.
